name: Mara Vale
execution_summary: I helped a volunteer group start a review pilot.
work_example: I recruited six reviewers, wrote the rubric, and ran two rounds of a pilot that processed 48 submissions. In round two I rewrote the handoff instructions after reviewers reported unclear ownership.
safety_gap: Small teams lose time repeating basic review setup. I would test a shared intake rubric on one batch and measure disagreements.
ambiguity: When nobody owned the review queue, I interviewed two reviewers, wrote a draft process, and volunteered to run the first round.
motivation: I want to apply my operations experience to making AI safety programs easier to run.

name: Ilan Moss
execution_summary: I owned the onboarding checklist and published it for a twelve-person workshop.
work_example: I maintained the checklist; the program lead recruited volunteers and ran the workshop.
safety_gap: New participants often need a clearer path from an event to a project.
ambiguity: I asked the program lead to choose between two formats.
motivation: I've volunteered with an AI safety reading group for two years and want to contribute through operations.

name: Tess Rowan
execution_summary: I led a three-person team to launch a mentor matching pilot.
work_example: I designed the intake form, assigned review shifts, and closed the pilot with 16 confirmed matches.
safety_gap: I would test better mentor handoffs before expanding the number of participants.
ambiguity: I cut the pilot scope after interviews showed that the original workflow was too time-consuming.
motivation: I'm interested in helping safety research groups run mentorship programs.

name: Noel Reed
execution_summary: I have an idea for a shared events directory.
work_example: I sketched the home page. It has not been shared with organizers.
ambiguity: I would ask an organizer what to build first.
motivation: I want to learn more about AI safety and meet practitioners.
